title: The word persuades through the Spirit, not beside it
source_text: XXVIII. Caeterum ut exponant quae sint in hac gratiae efficacia & operatione tum verbi Dei, tum Spiritus Sancti verbo utentis partes, dicunt verbum suadere, sed spiritum verbo utentem persuadere: ac praeterea tutius semper esse statuere, actionem spiritus, qua in voluntatem agit, sibi subordinatam habere actionem verbi, quam si actionem spiritus faciamus collateralem actioni verbi in voluntatem, & juxta verbum operari dicamus, non per verbum, ne Enthusiastis doctrinae suae principia, & nescio quos arcanos motus, tractiones, impulsus, quos facile quisque sibi imaginari potest, largiri videamur.
pass_a_gloss: XXVIII. But to set out what in this efficacy & operation of grace are the parts both of the word of God, and of the Holy Spirit using the word, they say that the word urges, but the spirit using the word persuades: and moreover that it is always safer to hold, that the action of the spirit, by which it acts on the will, has the action of the word subordinate to itself, than if we make the action of the spirit collateral with the action of the word on the will, & say that it works beside the word, not through the word, lest we seem to grant to the Enthusiasts the principles of their doctrine, & I know not what secret motions, drawings, impulses, which anyone can easily imagine for himself.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXVIII. To show what parts the word of God and the Holy Spirit who uses the word each play in this efficacy and working of grace, they say that the word urges but the Spirit using the word persuades.

They add that it is always safer to hold that the Spirit's action on the will has the word's action under it, than to make the Spirit's action run alongside the word's action on the will and say that he works beside the word rather than through it. This is so that we do not seem to hand the Enthusiasts the principles of their teaching, and who knows what hidden motions, drawings and impulses, which anyone can easily imagine for himself.
